description: Pre-registered attempts to fit and validate process components and model families on the normalized datasets published in this catalog. Splits, loader options, vintage policies and acceptance criteria are frozen here BEFORE any holdout result is read. A failing attempt is a result: it is kept, not re-specified. A change after seeing test outcomes must be added as a new attempt with a new id, a reason, and the superseded attempt left in place.
rules: Splits are chosen from data coverage only (first and last available period), never from outcomes.
Acceptance criteria are the component or family defaults declared in requirements.json; no attempt weakens them.
Entity selection rules (issuers, countries, symbols, regions) are declared here and use availability or pre-training-window counts only.

vintage_policy is the weakest policy the loaded sources support. 'retrospective' means timing leakage is controlled by the requirement's publication lag but revision leakage is possible, and the report says so.
Compute budget per attempt: 30 minutes wall clock. An attempt that exceeds it is recorded as not_run with reason compute_budget, not silently dropped.

delinquency_rate.description: Constructed: 100 * sum(bank_noncurrent_loans) / sum(bank_net_loans) over all FDIC-insured banks in the quarter. attempts.data: fred_macro_panel@normalized (FEDFUNDS, GDPC1, GDPPOT) + fred_cpi@normalized (CPIAUCSL), quarterly first releases
attempts.rationale: Supersedes the Okun-proxy attempt: the declared GDPC1/GDPPOT gap replaces it, at the rule's own quarterly frequency (rho is a quarterly smoothing parameter). Every input is its initial release, so no row contains a later revision and revisions are declared 'none'. Rows run 1995Q1-2024Q4 (120 quarters): train to 2007, validation 2008-2014, holdout 2015-2024 (40 quarters).
attempts.expected_limits: The gap is measured relative to its trailing 40-quarter mean inside one point-in-time snapshot, because ALFRED chained-dollar vintages carry no base-year metadata and a raw real-time level ratio produced gaps of +22% at benchmark revisions. A constant base offset cancels in logs; what remains is the gap relative to its recent average, which r_star absorbs. Inflation uses the quarter's first CPI month, the earliest print a real-time observer has.
attempts.contaminated: Built the output gap and inflation from per-period first releases across mixed bases, which forced a trailing-mean demeaning workaround. With per-vintage base_period the ratios are formed inside one base and the gap is a true level, so this pass was obtained on contaminated inputs and is superseded.

attempts.data: eia_energy@f5cd9308 (PET weekly WCESTUS1, WCRFPUS2, WCRIMUS2, WCREXUS2, WCRRIUS2; subject iso3:USA)
attempts.diagnosis: v1 failed interval_coverage alone (0.640 against 0.80 +/- 0.15) while beating persistence at p = 0.00093. The failure is a static predictive scale against strongly time-varying error volatility, not a too-narrow scale everywhere: over the holdout the mean predictive sd moves only 3,121 -> 3,380 while the realized one-step RMSE moves 4,473 (2020), 3,082 (2021), 6,113 (2022), 5,838 (2023), 3,243 (2024), and yearly coverage is 0.60/0.83/0.42/0.54/0.82. Within the training window the same expanding in-sample Gaussian scale OVER-covers (0.894-0.908 against 0.80) because 1991-1995 residuals (sd 4,563) inflate it relative to 2006-2010 (sd 1,562). Standardized holdout errors also have kurtosis 4.3 and are left-skewed (10% quantile -2.28, 90% +1.09).
attempts.interval_method: empirical_trailing, window 52 weeks, 40 quantile nodes, plus coefficient uncertainty x'Vx. The scale is the root mean square of the last 52 one-step residuals (one year, the petroleum stock cycle), and the shape is the empirical quantiles of residuals standardized by their own trailing scale, so tails and asymmetry are taken from the data rather than assumed. Chosen on training-window evidence only: over 1991-2019 the trailing Gaussian attains 0.789-0.796 coverage and the trailing empirical 0.797-0.808 at a nominal 0.80, against 0.894-0.908 for the expanding in-sample Gaussian.
attempts.rationale: Identical data, splits, vintage policy and acceptance criteria to inventory_balance.eia_weekly; the predictive distribution is the only change, so the two attempts are directly comparable.

attempts.data: fred_macro_panel@7dcce89c (TOTALSL), monthly
attempts.diagnosis: v2 failed interval_coverage alone (0.596) while beating persistence at p = 0.0022. The scored error is not the error the residuals measure. Under the strict real-time policy the forecast is anchored on the TOTALSL level available at the origin, while the actual is the latest vintage available at the evaluation cutoff, so the scored error contains the anchor level revision. TOTALSL log revisions from first release to latest have sd 0.0177 for 2013+ periods and 0.0348 for 1997-2012 (mean +0.070), against a model residual scale of 0.0057: realized standardized holdout errors have root mean square 3.73, and coverage bunches by year (0.00 in 2016 and 2022, 1.00 in 2014, 2018, 2019 and 2024) rather than scattering, which is the signature of one persistent revision episode per benchmark rather than of model noise. Excess kurtosis is small (3.78), so the tails are not the problem.
attempts.interval_method: gaussian_in_sample residual scale plus an independent data-revision component: the standard deviation of the log revisions the publisher has ALREADY made by the origin, over the most recent 60 mature periods, where mature means at least 12 months old. Twelve months is the shortest age at which a G.19 period has been through one annual benchmark, and five years keeps the estimate inside the current revision regime instead of averaging over the 2000s benchmark that moved the level about 5%. The mean revision is reported but deliberately NOT used to shift the point forecast, so any systematic revision bias stays visible in the bias statistic instead of being absorbed into the mechanism.
attempts.rationale: Identical data, splits, vintage policy and acceptance criteria to credit_growth.fred_realtime_v2.

attempts.data: census_business@5b0995c7 (County Business Patterns employment by state and NAICS sector)
attempts.diagnosis: v1 failed interval_coverage in the opposite direction (1.000 against 0.80 +/- 0.15) while halving the year-effect-only baseline error at p = 4.1e-06. The predictive sd of 0.0540 decomposes into a pooled within-year residual sd of 0.0201 and a between-year term of 0.0502; the between-year term is the variance of THREE year effects (-0.013, +0.071, +0.050) whose dispersion is the 2020 collapse and the 2021 rebound, added at full size as if the next year were a fresh draw. The within-year part is pooled across states whose own residual sds run from 0.0009 to 0.047, a factor of fifty, so one scale is simultaneously far too wide for stable states and too narrow for volatile ones. Realized 2023 cross-state error sd was 0.0115 with a common component of +0.0078.
attempts.interval_method: per_unit_year_mean: each state gets its own residual mean square shrunk toward the pooled one by a single prior observation (a three-year panel gives each state three residuals), and the common term becomes the sampling variance of the ESTIMATED year level (between-year variance / Y) rather than the variance of a fresh draw. Addresses the pooling defect directly; it cannot repair the common term, which three pandemic-era year effects cannot estimate.
attempts.rationale: Identical data, splits and acceptance criteria to regional_model.cbp_state_sectors.
attempts.expected_limits: With one holdout year, all 51 forecasts share one draw of the common component, so interval_coverage here is one Bernoulli trial and not a coverage estimate. regional_model.qcew_state_sectors is registered below to make the criterion evaluable on a longer panel with six holdout years. no_revision_leakage fails as in v1: CBP publishes no vintages.

attempts.data: bls_labor@ffd7f43a (QCEW annual-average private employment, state x NAICS 2-digit sector, aggregation level 54, 2005-2024)
attempts.entity_rule: Every state-equivalent QCEW publishes at aggregation level 54 (50 states, DC and Puerto Rico; 53 areas), and every two-digit NAICS private sector. Selection is availability only.
attempts.rationale: The declared fix for the CBP attempt: the rebuilt bls_labor (60.9M rows) carries QCEW annual averages from 1990, so the panel has twenty years and nineteen growth years instead of four and three. Base-year shares are 2005, the validation targets are 2015-2018 and the holdout is 2019-2024, six years x 53 areas, so the between-year component is estimated from thirteen year effects at the first holdout origin and interval_coverage is evaluated over six independent common draws instead of one. QCEW labels each year with the NAICS revision in force, so two-digit sector codes are compared across revisions and the published namespaces are recorded.

The holdout deliberately contains 2020 and 2021, which no interval method can anticipate; that is the point of scoring six years rather than one.
attempts.superseded_reason: WS-E interval calibration, 2026-09-17: see the sixth_wave note and docs/research-log/ws-e-interval-coverage.md.

attempts.data: mit_election_returns@017e0d4f (U.S. House district general-election returns 1976-2024) + fec_candidates@a46824fd (candidate master: office, state, district, party, CAND_ICI) + fec@93722c10 (weball candidate cycle receipts) + fred_macro_panel@7dcce89c (DSPIC96 ALFRED vintages)
attempts.entity_rule: Every U.S. House district-cycle general election (no primaries, no special elections) for which all declared inputs exist: a two-party result, a partisan lean from a contested result within the previous three cycles, an FEC candidate record for the cycle, and a national income growth reading published on election day. Availability only.
attempts.split_rule: By ELECTION YEAR, so no future election can inform a past prediction: fit through 2016, validate 2018-2020, test 2022-2024. Each holdout origin refits on cycles up to and including the previous one.

district_presidential_lean.source_series: MEDSL U.S. House district returns, previous contested cycle
district_presidential_lean.description: Substitutes for the declared district presidential lean. No published dataset in this catalog provides presidential vote by congressional district: mit_election_returns publishes county and statewide presidential returns, and counties do not nest inside congressional districts. pvi is instead the district two-party Democratic share in its most recent contested cycle within three cycles, minus the national two-party Democratic House share of that same cycle.

fred_economy.description: Substitutes for the declared A229RX0 (real disposable personal income per capita), which fred_macro_panel does not publish. econ is the twelve-month growth of real disposable personal income read from the ALFRED vintage available ON election day, with both endpoints on one base period.

attempts.rationale: The elections family was blocked on data until mit_election_returns published House district returns. The target is the contested district two-party Democratic share in the next cycle given realized fundamentals; the secondary declared group is the Democratic seat count. Baselines: persistence (the district previous share), historical_mean (its pre-origin mean) and the supplied incumbent_party_holds rule (every seat stays with the party holding it, at that party average holding share; for seats, the current split). Acceptance is the family default plus the declared beats_district_mean_dm.
attempts.expected_limits: Three timing caveats are declared rather than hidden. (1) FEC weball receipts are cycle-to-date totals whose coverage ends after election day (2000: 2001-06-30 ... 2024: 2025-01-30), so fundraising is a conditional input: the holdout tests the mechanism given realized fundraising, not the ability to forecast it. (2) Receipts are summed over all of a party candidates in the district-cycle, including primary losers. (3) Redistricting changes what a district number means in 2002, 2012 and 2022, so the lagged lean crosses a boundary change in those cycles; the family already declares this. Fusion-party lines (New York, Connecticut) are not credited to the major party they endorse, which is how MEDSL publishes them. Row dates are election days and certified returns are not revised, so revisions are declared none.
attempts.run_note: CORRECTION (2026-09-16, before any holdout was scored): five district-cycles have a negative party receipts total, because a weball cycle total can be negative when a candidate refunds more than they raise. worldmodel.models.elections requires a nonnegative amount and refused to fit at all, so the loader clamps a negative party total to zero and counts the clamps in construction.clamped. AL-05 2014, FL-19 2012, MD-07 2022, TN-06 2016 and TN-06 2022 are affected. No result existed when this was corrected.

attempts.data: fred_macro_panel@normalized (DPRIME) + fred_policy_rate@normalized (DFF), monthly means of daily vintages
attempts.diagnosis: v1 failed interval_coverage alone (0.988 against 0.80 +/- 0.15) while halving persistence's error at p = 0.0011. The predictive scale is an average across monetary-policy regimes, not a forecast of the current one. At the validation cutoff the in-sample residual scale is 0.2217 while the residual root mean square by decade is 0.1560 (1950s), 0.1796 (1960s), 0.2539 (1970s), 0.4186 (1980s), 0.1142 (1990s), 0.0816 (2000s) and 0.0416 (2010s) -- a tenfold spread, with the flat scale set mostly by the Volcker era. A 2005 ALFRED vintage of DPRIME publishes its history back to 1955, so the expanding in-sample scale carries that era into every forecast. This is visible before the holdout: in the SELECTION window (2013-2017, 59 forecasts) the default over-covers at 1.000 with a mean predictive sd of 0.2259 against a realized RMSE of 0.0498. The in-sample standardized errors also have kurtosis 6.0, which is what a rate that moves in discrete 25bp steps looks like: a spike at zero change with occasional jumps, not a Gaussian.
attempts.interval_method: empirical_trailing, window 120 months, 40 quantile nodes. The scale is the root mean square of the last 120 one-step residuals and the shape is the empirical quantiles of residuals standardized by their own trailing scale, so the discrete-step tails are taken from the data rather than assumed. No coefficient-uncertainty or revision component is declared: DPRIME is not revised and 746 residuals against 5 coefficients make x'Vx negligible, so neither is part of the diagnosis. Candidate interval methods are compared on the SELECTION window only (train_end -> validation_end, evaluated at validation_end, the same view validate_process uses to select candidates) and the declared rule is LOWEST VALIDATION-WINDOW CRPS, a proper score that is blind to interval coverage. Choosing the candidate whose coverage sits closest to 0.80 would be tuning to the acceptance criterion and was not used. Validation-window CRPS over the declared candidate grid (four methods x windows 36/60/120): gaussian_in_sample 0.05714; gaussian_trailing 0.02954 (36), 0.02945 (60), 0.02944 (120); student_t_trailing 0.03023 (60); empirical_trailing 0.02495 (36), 0.02497 (60), 0.02207 (120). The rule selects empirical_trailing at window 120, whose validation coverage (0.9153) is the WORST of the three trailing windows (0.8983 at 36, 0.8814 at 60) -- the evidence that CRPS and not coverage did the selecting.

attempts.data: fred_macro_panel@7dcce89c (PAYEMS, INDPRO across all index bases), monthly
attempts.diagnosis: With the conditional-input correction in force (v3) the remaining interval defect is the one credit_growth had: under the strict real-time policy the forecast is anchored on the PAYEMS level available at the origin while the actual is the latest vintage available at the evaluation cutoff, so the scored error carries the anchor's later benchmark revision, which is part of no in-sample residual. Measured at the validation cutoff, PAYEMS log revisions from first release to latest have a root mean square of 0.00458 for 2000s periods against a model residual scale of 0.00304 -- the revision component is larger than the residual it is being added to. In the SELECTION window the default under-covers at 0.600 with a mean predictive sd of 414.5 thousand against a realized RMSE of 767.2, and standardized errors have root mean square 1.86.
attempts.interval_method: gaussian_in_sample residual scale plus an independent data-revision component: the standard deviation of the log revisions the publisher has ALREADY made by the origin, over the most recent 120 mature periods, where mature means at least 24 months old. Twenty-four months is the age at which a CES period has been through both its level benchmark (published with January data each February, revising from the previous March forward) and the following year's seasonal-factor revision. Ten years keeps the estimate inside the current benchmark methodology instead of averaging over the 1950s, whose log-revision root mean square is 0.0185 against 0.0046 in the 2000s. The mean revision is reported and deliberately not used to shift the point forecast, so systematic revision bias stays visible in the bias statistic. Candidate interval methods are compared on the SELECTION window only (train_end -> validation_end, evaluated at validation_end, the same view validate_process uses to select candidates) and the declared rule is LOWEST VALIDATION-WINDOW CRPS, a proper score that is blind to interval coverage. Choosing the candidate whose coverage sits closest to 0.80 would be tuning to the acceptance criterion and was not used. Validation-window CRPS over the declared candidates: default 440.1; +revision 431.0; gaussian_trailing(60) 489.5; gaussian_trailing(60)+revision 437.5; gaussian_trailing(120)+revision 437.6; empirical_trailing(60)+revision 434.9; empirical_trailing(120)+revision 437.0. The rule selects the revision component alone. The heteroskedasticity argument that fixed interest_pass_through is real here too (residual root mean square 0.0065 in the 1940s against 0.0011 in the 1990s) but points the other way: a trailing scale NARROWS this interval (mean sd 206.1 against 414.5) and drives validation coverage down to 0.358, so it is not adopted.

attempts.diagnosis: v1 failed interval_coverage from below (0.597) while beating the year-effect-only baseline at p = 1.2e-04. The year-by-year pattern says where the failure lives: 0.85 (2019), 0.04 (2020), 0.38 (2021), 0.45 (2022), 0.98 (2023), 0.89 (2024). Outside the pandemic the intervals are roughly right; 2020-2022 is a structural break, and the conditional shift-share shock carried the industry composition of the collapse while each state's deviation from it was far larger than nineteen pre-pandemic years of state residuals can price. That is not a misspecified variance component, so the honest expectation registered here is that no interval method repairs it. See the 'correction' field for the decomposition argument this attempt was first registered on and the evidence that refutes it.
attempts.interval_method: per_unit_year_draw: per_unit_year_mean's per-region within-year residual variance (each region's own residual mean square shrunk toward the pooled one by a single prior observation, declared because region residual sds span a factor of fifty) paired with the fresh-draw common term between x (1 + 1/Y) of the pooled default. Selection is by the same declared rule as every other WS-E attempt -- lowest validation-window CRPS, a proper score blind to coverage -- computed over the three declared regional methods on the 2015-2018 selection window; the numbers are recorded in docs/research-log/ws-e-interval-coverage.md next to the verdict.

attempts.correction: 2026-09-17, recorded BEFORE the holdout was scored and kept because the reasoning is part of the result. This attempt was first registered on an a-priori decomposition argument: the forecast error contains next year's own common shock, so the predictive variance of the common component should be between x (1 + 1/Y) (a fresh draw plus the sampling error of the mean of Y past effects) rather than per_unit_year_mean's between / Y (the sampling variance of an estimated level). THAT ARGUMENT IS WRONG FOR THIS DESIGN, and the evidence that refutes it was available without touching the holdout. The shift-share shock is built from REALIZED other-region industry employment at the target year -- a declared conditional input -- so log(others_after / others_before) already contains the target year's common component. What is left to forecast is therefore much closer to an estimated level than to a fresh draw. On the synthetic shift-share panel in tests (16 years, 30 regions, a genuine common year shock of sd 0.004 and region noise spanning twentyfold), per_unit_year_mean attains coverage 0.8000 against a nominal 0.80 while per_unit_year_draw over-covers at 0.8417 and pooled_year_draw at 0.8667 -- so on a correctly specified generator the fresh-draw term double-counts a shock the conditional input already carries. The fifth wave's choice of per_unit_year_mean was right. This attempt is run anyway, under the same declared lowest-validation-CRPS rule as every other WS-E attempt, so that the comparison is on the record rather than asserted.

attempts.correction: 2026-09-17: an inconsistency inside the code, not a re-specification of the mechanism. The Hawkes recursion gives the conditional MEAN of a country-month count; the holdout forecaster set sd = sqrt(mean), which asserts that the count is equidispersed Poisson. This family's own simulator does not assert that -- worldmodel.models.conflict.simulate draws counts as negative_binomial(rng, lambda, dispersion), and 'dispersion' (nb2_alpha) is a declared family parameter with bounds [0, 50]. fit_hawkes never estimated it, so it stayed at its default 0 and the score was Poisson while the simulator was negative binomial. fit_hawkes now estimates it by method of moments on the fit window's own residuals, alpha = sum[(N-lambda)^2 - lambda] / sum[lambda^2], and the forecaster uses Var = lambda + alpha lambda^2. alpha = 0 reproduces sqrt(mean) exactly, so this is not a widening factor: it is the dispersion the family already declared, measured instead of assumed.
attempts.diagnosis: v1 failed interval_coverage at 0.596 along with beats_persistence_dm (p = 0.58) and no_revision_leakage. The coverage failure is the equidispersion assumption and the evidence is direct: over the fit-plus-validation window (4,300 one-step country-month forecasts, holdout untouched) the Poisson Pearson dispersion mean[(N-lambda)^2/lambda] is 35.9 against the 1.0 the Poisson score assumes, and the NB2 moment estimate of alpha is 0.041. Conflict counts cluster within a month beyond what a monthly excitation kernel can carry, which is the standard reason event counts are overdispersed.
attempts.interval_method: Unchanged shape, corrected dispersion: the predictive stays Gaussian around the Hawkes intensity, as in v1, and only its standard deviation changes from sqrt(lambda) to sqrt(lambda + alpha lambda^2) with alpha estimated at each refit from pre-origin residuals. Changing the shape as well would be a second, separately arguable change and was not made.

sixth_wave: 2026-09-17, WS-E. interval_coverage blocked 16 of the 35 attempts, more than any other criterion, and needs no new data. Each of the 16 was diagnosed separately into one of two causes the record already distinguishes: a SCORING BUG (a real-time forecast graded against a later vintage, as credit_growth was) or GENUINE MISCALIBRATION (the predictive distribution is the wrong shape or the wrong width for the right reason). One new scoring bug was found and fixed in the code: the backtest handed a declared conditional input's value at the target period from the evaluation vintage while its own lag in the same design row came from the origin's vintage, so labor_demand's output-growth regressor was the INDPRO rebasing factor (-0.2177) rather than realized growth (+0.0005). Components now declare conditional_rebase per input; only labor_demand declares one, and the other six conditional inputs were measured and left unchanged. The regional family gains per_unit_year_draw, which pairs per_unit_year_mean's per-region within-year scale with the fresh-draw common term the default already used, because between/Y is the predictive variance of a year effect treated as a fixed level and the forecast error contains next year's own draw. Every candidate interval method was compared on the SELECTION window under a declared rule of lowest CRPS -- a proper score, blind to coverage -- and no threshold was relaxed. Attempts with no principled fix are recorded as still failing: see docs/research-log/ws-e-interval-coverage.md for the count and the reason for each.
